title: Should a musician leave music for management?
summary: Pressed by Hinton, Thomas says in hindsight he would have kept writing.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Advice to young musicians starting out

blocks.x: Now, this combination of this whole (?) is to give some advice to young people that are listening to your story and about your life, and what happened to you, and what accomplishments you've done... Look here, what have you got to say to them that would help them not make some of the mistakes that you've made and some of the mistakes that I've made? How can they get into this?
Would you advise a young musician after a certain age to change from being a young musician to going to booking or personal management? What would you do?
Well, I'd advise them to learn where the clubs and things are, and to book...

Would you advise them to stop playing music to do that? That's what I'm trying to say? You were a talented musician, and you got up to be assistant director of one of the biggest bands in America, Cab Calloway's band, and then all of a sudden you stopped playing. You were one of the Black musicians to really study and learn to play properly, and then all of a sudden you stopped playing and went into another facet of the business. Would you advise a young person to do that?
Not necessarily. Because I'm very disgusted about my side of it that I didn't just keep writing. Because I still could have made a career in writing, because...
What would you suggest to young people who are talented? How are you going to help them, so they can say, well, okay, this is what we're going to do now?

Well, one thing that they have to know is what the business is like and what to do with the business. Because if you get the nucleus of artists that is sellable, that you're going to record them and get a record... See, it's through exposure and publicity that an artist is worth any money. Because I did that...I proved that... We had a

hard time talking Domino into getting a publicity man. I did that for Bill Doggett and Bill Davis, and got them publicity, and it upped their salary. But you've got to get a guy that will stay with you...

But do you think that leaving the music to go into managerial... Is it worth that for somebody that has spent as much time as you spent to learn how to write and to arrange? Is it worth that to change and to go into...
Okay, that's what I'm trying to get. That's why I want to know what you've got to suggest to young people.
